Where the data comes from

California mails a ballot to every registered voter. Each day, the California Secretary of State publishes a vote-by-mail ballot report for all 58 counties: how many ballots were issued, how many have come back (and whether by mail, drop box, drop-off location or vote center), and how many the county has accepted.

Each report is a running total through 11:59 PM the night before it posts. VoteFlow checks for a new one every hour and keeps every report, so the change from one report to the next shows what each county added that day. Counties log ballots as they process them, which can trail the day a voter returned one, and a count occasionally goes down when a county corrects an earlier figure. Those changes are shown as reported.

Registered voter counts come from the state's Report of Registration. The daily history here starts with the report for October 11, about a week after ballots went out.

After Election Day, the state also publishes estimates of ballots still waiting to be counted in each county. VoteFlow will add those to show how quickly each county works through its ballots.

Why California?

California is the biggest vote-by-mail state in the country, with more than 23 million ballots in the mail for this election.

The Secretary of State publishes nice tables and charts, but I wanted to analyze the data further: day by day and county by county, how fast ballots are coming back, how voters are returning them, and how quickly counties are processing them.

VoteFlow started in Virginia, where I have the most election experience. California is the second state.

Why this site exists

Hi, I'm Ravi Udeshi. I'm an election administrator who loves technology and building things.

When I worked in a local Virginia elections office, I was always curious how early voting was unfolding day by day. I kept detailed spreadsheets of the daily numbers, compared them with past elections, and tried to project where turnout might end up and how busy the days ahead would be.

VoteFlow is the modern version of those spreadsheets, for every locality in Virginia and every county in California. It updates automatically throughout the day.

There are no ads or sponsorships here. It's a passion project, made to be useful to election administrators and anyone else who's curious about elections data.

If there's something you'd like to see added, send me an email, and maybe I can add it!
